report.what_happened:
On 19 December 2025 the clinic billed Granite Peak Health under the medical benefit for a pembrolizumab infusion [[raw:106]], and the clearinghouse accepted it for processing on 20 December 2025 [[raw:107]]. The payer's first remittance, on 15 January 2026 [[raw:148]], paid the claim in full at $32,436.00 [[calc:reimbursement.expected_usd]], and a matching deposit from Granite Peak Health had posted on 14 January 2026 [[raw:297]]; matched on amount and date alone, the episode closed on 1 February 2026 [[verdict:B-04]]. There is no 340B rebate track on this episode.

Then a second, identical deposit posted on 2 February 2026 [[raw:306]], and on 19 February 2026 a second remittance arrived for the same claim under a different payer claim number — 20260613585152 rather than 20260612768572 [[raw:153]]. That remittance matched the second deposit by its payment reference, and on 1 March 2026 the episode reopened from CLOSED [[verdict:B-16]].
report.why_it_is_open: The episode is open because the payer sent the same 835 twice and both payments landed. The engine expects one payment of $32,436.00 [[calc:reimbursement.expected_usd]] and sees $64,872.00 received [[calc:reimbursement.received_usd]] — one full payment over, a variance of -$32,436.00 [[calc:reimbursement.variance_usd]]. That is a duplicate 835 for the same claim [B-16], carried under reason code DUPLICATE_REMITTANCE, and the episode now sits in EXCEPTION.
report.what_i_could_not_determine: Nothing — every question this episode raises is answered by the records above.
report.what_a_human_should_check_first:
- Compare the two payer claim numbers, 20260612768572 and 20260613585152, and confirm both describe the same service rather than a re-adjudication that should replace the first remittance.
- Confirm with the bank whether the second $32,436.00 deposit of 2 February 2026 [[raw:306]] is still sitting in the account as an overpayment.
